slides.title: What Are Multi-Dimensional Arrays
slides.content: Multi-dimensional arrays store data in a grid-like structure. A 2D array uses two indices: row and column.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: How many dimensions does int[,] have?

slides.title: Declaring and Initializing 2D Arrays
slides.content: You can declare a 2D array with new int[rows, cols] or initialize it with values directly.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Complete the declaration: int[,] board = new int[3, _____];

slides.title: Accessing 2D Array Elements
slides.content: Elements are accessed using two indices: matrix[row, col]. The first index is the row, the second is the column.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Drag the correct syntax to get row 0, column 1 from grid: grid[?, ?]

slides.title: Iterating Over 2D Arrays
slides.content: Nested for loops are commonly used to traverse every element in a 2D array.

exercise.prompt: Write the inner loop condition to iterate columns of a 2x2 array.
exercise.expectedOutput: A valid condition like 2 or grid.GetLength(1)
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: j <
When run, your code should output: A valid condition like 2 or grid.GetLength(1)

slides.title: What Are Jagged Arrays
slides.content: Jagged arrays are arrays of arrays. Each inner array can have a different length, unlike 2D arrays.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Which syntax defines a jagged array?

slides.title: Accessing Jagged Array Elements
slides.content: Jagged arrays use two pairs of brackets. First for the outer array, second for the inner array.
slides.example:
int[][] jagged = { new[] {1, 2}, new[] {3} };
int x = jagged[0][1]; // 2
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

slides.title: 2D vs Jagged Arrays
slides.content: 2D arrays have a fixed rectangular shape. Jagged arrays allow irregular rows but have slightly more overhead.
slides.example:
int[,] rect = new int[2, 3]; // always 2x3
int[][] jag = new int[2][]; // rows can differ
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Drag the correct array type when each row can have a different length: [?]

slides.title: Multi-Dimensional Arrays Review
slides.content: Use int[,] for fixed grids and int[][] for irregular data. Both support indexing and iteration.

exercise.prompt: Declare a 2x3 int 2D array and assign 7 to row 1, column 2.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: new int[2, 3]
When run, your code should output: 7
